title: Rollout Conductivity Lab — Notes & Checklist (Aug 2027)
content:
Purpose and quick summary:
This doc captures an experiment-style rollout 'conductivity' lab for a mid-scope feature (routing + small model swap) intended to exercise our throttles, KV-cache warmup behavior, and cross-region fallbacks before a wider Dedicated release. The goal: make small, measurable increases to traffic while intentionally stimulating friction points so the ops path and telemetry surface early.

Audience:
- Release engineers and launch operators
- Serving-runtime oncall and SRE
- Product engineering owning the model variant
- Solutions Eng for customer-impact checks

High-level approach (why "conductivity"):
Treat the rollout like a materials test: we want to measure the system's ability to transmit load without creating hotspots. Instead of a single canary, we run three microcohorts, each exercising a distinct axis:
  - cohort A (local latency focus): small % routed to new model in us-west for latency SLO verification
  - cohort B (load distribution): bursty weight to multiple regions to validate smart routing and burst capacity
  - cohort C (cache/throughput): long-running sessions to stress KV cache and batching kernels

Key metrics to surface (with quick thresholds):
  - P95 latency (gen endpoint): warn if > baseline + 60ms; critical if > baseline + 150ms
  - Error rate (5xx and model mismatches): warn if > 0.5% spike; critical if > 2% sustained over 5m
  - Token cost per request (sampling): alert if > baseline + 20% (unexpected token regressions)
  - Queue/backlog length on serving pods: warn if > 30% of concurrency headroom
  - KV cache hit ratio: warn if drops below 70% for cohort C
  - Autoscaler downscale throttle events: early signal of instability

Preflight checklist (must be green before traffic flows):
  1) Config review: rollout policy, fallback route map, model pin version checked (owner: Priya)
  2) Telemetry hooks: sampling slices for cohort tagging added (owner: Lina)
  3) Synthetic smoke tests: 50 endpoints in each region pass (owner: Marcos)
  4) Canary image pinned and verified in staging registry (owner: Release Infra)
  5) Ops channels: #release-watch & #serving-ops muted alert rules set; pager oncall notified (owner: Evan)
  6) Rollout calendar published + shift rota (see calendar block)
  7) Backout plan confirmed and tested in dry-run (owner: SRE)

Staged calendar (48h compact lab) — concise timeline:
  Day 0 (T-2 days): preflight, config review, synthetic runs, dry-backout rehearsal
  Day 1 09:00 UTC: open watch window, cohort A -> 0.5% for 10m; observe 30m
  Day 1 10:30 UTC: cohort A -> 2% for 20m if stable; cohort B -> 0.2% burst for 5m every 15m
  Day 1 13:00 UTC: cohort C begin (long sessions) ramp 0.1% -> 0.5% over 2 hours
  Day 1 18:00 UTC: consolidation window, freeze increases, aggregate telemetry
  Day 2 09:00 UTC: decision meeting (30m) — escalate to wider canary or rollback

Decision gates (what to watch during windows):
  - Gate 1 (initial): no P95 regression beyond warn threshold and no >1% error spike
  - Gate 2 (post-burst): stable queue/backlog and no autoscaler oscillation
  - Gate 3 (sustained): KV cache hit ratio holds and sample output quality (quick eval set) passes basic checks
If any gate fails, immediate rollback to previous routing policy and inform customer success for customers in cohort.

Operator run-commands (quick cheatsheet):
  - Pause rollout: POST /api/rollouts/{id}/pause (ops UI also available)
  - Rollback to tag: infra-cli rollback --service-generation=<prev-gen> --reason="conductivity-fail"
  - Increase logging for a pod: kubectl annotate pod/<pod> debug-logs=true --namespace=serving
  - Trigger synthetic: /ops/synthetics/run?profile=conductivity-smoke

Telemetry and alert tuning notes:
  - Create temporary split metrics: rollout.cohort=A/B/C so we can slice alarms; TTL 7 days
  - Add low-frequency trace sampling for cohort C to capture KV cold miss flows
  - Add an ephemeral dashboard with baseline overlays (30m, 2h) and save as Draft: "Conductivity Lab — Aug 2027"
  - Relax some noisy page rules (e.g., minor token-cost increases) to avoid pager fatigue, but keep slack-critical channels enabled

Sample rollout checklist (ops on watch):
  - 00:00 Start watch window, confirm oncall, confirm links in slack header
  - +10m, +30m, +60m: quick thumbs-up posts from SRE, Serving, and Product (explicitly: "ok to continue")
  - Record anomalies immediately in the rolllog thread with timestamps and stack traces
  - If rolling back, mark the timeline entry and take a retro snapshot of metrics at rollback timestamp

Rollback scenarios (graded):
  - Soft rollback (fast): stop increment and move traffic back to previous model variant routing (expected < 3m to complete for most routes)
  - Hard rollback (emergency): full routing policy switch and scale down new pool, evacuate KV cache lanes (expected 10–15m)
  - Post-rollback activities: hold a 1h triage, preserve traces and logs for 7 days, open a postmortem ticket if customer-impacting

Quality checks and sample evals (quick):
  - Run 200 random samples from production traffic subset through the new model variant and compare: hallucination rate, hallucination severity score (team: NLP QE)
  - Run unit prompt sets for known customer-critical scenarios (owner: Solutions Eng)

Open questions / risks to track:
  - Risk: prefix caching warmup may produce temporary latency spikes for long-tailed sessions — mitigate by cohort C slow ramp
  - Question: do we want to enable quantized kernel path for cohort B? (Pros: cost; Cons: unknown quality impact)
  - Risk: cross-region fallback could create asymmetric load on europe-west if us-east churns — ensure region-weight cap in policy

Action items before next rehearsal:
  - Lina: finalize cohort tagging and ephemeral dashboard (due 2027-08-17)
  - Marcos: run extended synthetic with KV miss storm profile in staging (due 2027-08-17)
  - Priya: confirm customer exclusion list and notify affected accounts (due 2027-08-16)
  - Evan: publish calendar and shift rota, post links to #release-watch (done 2027-08-15)

Retro template (post-lab):
  - What happened (short timeline)
  - Signals and where they tripped (metric + timestamp)
  - Root cause hypothesis (if any)
  - What we changed mid-flight and why
  - Action items and owners
  - Small wins (what behaved better than expected)

Notes to self (quick, informal):
  - Keep this lab rhythmic and short — it's exploratory, not a migration.
  - Use the lab to validate observability primitives we want in the bigger Dedicated launch.
  - If telemetry sampling shows unexpected model regression, pause before escalating traffic.

Appendix: useful links and quick references
  - Rollout tool UI: https://console.redwood.ai/rollouts
  - Synthetic runner: https://ops.redwood.ai/synthetics
  - Pager rota: https://schedules.redwood.ai/serving-oncall

End of doc.
